display.purpose: The Nerve wordmark only: Bricolage Grotesque at its display optical size and 94% width, followed by the fleet pane.

name.purpose: Agent and speaker names in the chat header, top-level session rows and message headers. The operator's name takes Cantaloupe text.

headline.purpose: Section titles on settings and dialog surfaces.

title.purpose: Panel header labels, field labels, Send, table heads. Sentence case.

body.purpose: Agent prose on the 34em reading measure (about 68 characters).

ui.purpose: Chips, list rows, inputs, toolbar buttons and tree entries.

label.purpose: Status bar, metadata, hints, badges and intermediate assistant messages.

mono.purpose: Tool rows, timestamps, durations, model names and code; tabular numerals always on.

shadows.name: plate-shadow
shadows.purpose: Edge light on every plate, tool stack and the active segmented chip. Daylight: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border).

shadows.name: plate-shadow-operator
shadows.purpose: Warm edge light on the operator's message plate. Daylight: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-operator) 45%, var(--border)).

shadows.name: float-shadow
shadows.purpose: The composer and the command palette shell: the only surfaces that float. Daylight: 0 14px 36px rgba(19, 23, 34, 0.14), 0 1px 2px rgba(19, 23, 34, 0.08), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--border).

shadows.name: menu-shadow
shadows.purpose: Inline select listboxes, slash menus and top bar panels.

shadows.name: pane-edge
shadows.purpose: The window frame of a dark pane; removed when the pane lights.

motion.name: switch-duration
motion.purpose: Every state switch: pane colour, hover fill, border colour, Send brightness. Never looped.

motion.name: switch-ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve, used for switches and entrances alike.

motion.name: enter-fast
motion.purpose: Fade or slide-down entrance for search bars and menus.

motion.name: enter-message
motion.purpose: Opacity fade when a message enters the transcript.

motion.name: enter-drawer
motion.purpose: Settings drawer slide-in from the right.

motion.name: send-pulse
motion.purpose: Send flashes brighter once when a message leaves.

motion.name: streaming-cursor
motion.purpose: The only looping animation: a small live pane at the end of streaming text. Stopped under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion makes every switch and entrance instant.

breakpoints.name: topbar-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Below this chips and icon buttons drop to a 40px minimum.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: controls grow to a 44px touch minimum and inputs use 16px text.

breakpoints.name: compact-layout
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: the three columns collapse to one with panel toggles in the top bar.

narrative.overview:
An operator's console is a building seen at night. You do not read the facade by its architecture; you read it by which rooms are lit and how warm the light is. Nerve borrows that reading. Cold electric blue is an agent at work. Warm cantaloupe is the operator, and anything that has finished and now waits on the operator. When work is done the window goes dark. Colour never decorates, it reports, and because every lit surface means something, the shell can hold a whole fleet in a glance without asking for attention.

The mood is midnight, exact, calm, dense, lit. This is an Operate-mode surface that stays open for hours, so the brand lives in precise details rather than expression: a 28px row unit shared by every list row, tool row and panel header; plates that read by value and a 1px edge light instead of drawn borders; one display face reserved for the wordmark and the names of agents and speakers; prose held to a 68-character measure. Density is welcome because nothing pulses, glows or gradients. State changes are a light switch, 120ms, on or off.

The system refuses the hacker costume (scanlines, glowing HUD chrome, tracked uppercase labels), the grey dashboard with one decorative accent, glass and gradients, coloured side rails, and any pulsing or breathing motion. Daylight is the same building by day: cool paper, printed hairlines instead of edge light, panes printed as ink swatches, identical meanings. The previous appearance survives only as an opt-in Classic skin scoped under its own attribute and is not part of this system.
keyCharacteristics: Light temperature is the state vocabulary: blue works, cantaloupe waits on you, red failed, dark is done.
Flat lit panes (10x14 default, 8x11 small, 14x20 facade) are the only state marker; no glows, dots, rails or glyph icons.
One 28px row unit across list rows, tool rows, panel headers and the status bar; the top bar is 44px.
Raised plates read by tonal value plus a 1px top edge light; only floating surfaces cast a real offset shadow.
Corners stay between 1px and 4px; larger radius steps clamp to 4px.
Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for reading and UI, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular numerals for measures, Bricolage Grotesque for names only.
Sentence case everywhere; no eyebrows, kickers or tracked caps.
Motion is a 120ms switch with a near-linear ease-out; reduced motion makes it instant.

rules.name: The Light Temperature Rule
rules.body: Blue is agent work, cantaloupe is the operator and anything waiting on the operator, red is error, and nothing else is coloured. A surface that is not reporting one of those three states is a neutral.

rules.name: The Names Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is used only for the wordmark and for agent or speaker names. Headings, labels and buttons stay in Atkinson.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, header, chip and button is sentence case. No eyebrows, no kickers above headings, no letterspaced capitals.

rules.name: The One Row Rule
rules.body: Every list row, tool row, panel header and the status bar sits on the 1.867rem (28px) row unit; density comes from sharing one rhythm, not from shrinking it.

rules.name: The Edge Light Rule
rules.body: Plates read by value and a 1px top highlight, not by drawn borders; Daylight prints a hairline instead. Drawn borders are reserved for inputs, outline buttons and hairline dividers.

rules.name: The Switch Rule
rules.body: State changes switch in 120ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`; nothing breathes or pulses, and reduced motion makes every transition and animation instant. Entrances (messages, menus, drawers) fade or slide once in 140ms to 220ms using the same ease.

dos: **Do** show state only with a lit pane: Electric Blue for agent work, Cantaloupe for the operator and work waiting on the operator, Signal Red for failure, Pane Off when done (The Light Temperature Rule).
**Do** switch panes and hover fills in 120ms with `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` and let reduced motion make them instant (The Switch Rule).
**Do** build raised surfaces as plates: Panel fill plus the 1px edge light, no drawn border; in Daylight the token prints a hairline (The Edge Light Rule).
**Do** keep every list row, tool row, panel header and the status bar on the 1.867rem row unit (The One Row Rule).
**Do** reserve Bricolage Grotesque for the wordmark and agent or speaker names (The Names Rule).
**Do** hold agent prose to the 34em reading measure and let code, tables and charts take the column.
**Do** set timestamps, counts, durations, models and code in Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono with tabular numerals.
**Do** keep corners between 1px and 4px; 6px is only for the floating command palette shell.
**Do** make Send the one warm control on a screen: Cantaloupe fill, Midnight label, 3px radius.
**Do** give every pane without adjacent text an accessible label (Running, Waiting on you, Failed, Idle).
donts: **Don't** colour anything that is not reporting agent work, operator ownership or an error; no decorative accents, coloured side rails or tinted headers.
**Don't** pulse, breathe, glow or animate a shadow; the only blinking element is the streaming cursor pane, and it stops under reduced motion.
**Don't** add scanlines, HUD chrome, letterspaced uppercase labels, eyebrows or kickers above headings; labels are sentence case.
**Don't** use glass, blur, gradients or zero-offset shadows; depth is tonal value plus the edge light, and only floating surfaces cast an offset shadow.
**Don't** draw a border around a plate; borders belong to inputs, outline buttons and hairline dividers.
**Don't** replace a pane with a dot, a circle, a badge or a glyph icon, and never make colour the only signal.
**Don't** use Bricolage Grotesque for headings, labels or buttons, or a system display face anywhere.
**Don't** round panels or shell surfaces beyond 4px, or reintroduce the Classic skin's rounded panels and amber accents into the Nerve style.
